record.oneLiner: The famous feathered 'first bird', a transitional Jurassic dinosaur.
record.description: Archaeopteryx is a famous bird-like dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of southern Germany, long regarded as the earliest known bird. About the size of a magpie (up to ~50 cm long), it combined feathers and wings with reptilian features — toothed jaws, clawed fingers and a long bony tail — a classic transitional fossil between non-avian dinosaurs and birds.

notableFacts.text: A classic transitional fossil between non-avian dinosaurs and birds.
Its preserved feathers were among the first evidence linking birds to dinosaurs.
Combined bird-like feathers and wings with dinosaur teeth, clawed fingers and a bony tail.
